title: How can the four sides of a rectangle be written shorter?
description: The four sides of a rectangle are added as l plus b plus l plus b. The same letters are put together to make a shorter sum, and the short form is checked with a length of three and a breadth of four. Keeko's doubt is that the four sides give four times l times b.
teaching_notes: One idea: adding a letter to itself gives two times that letter, so l plus l plus b plus b becomes two l plus two b. Watch for students who multiply the letters instead of adding them.

source: A rectangle has length l and breadth b. Write its perimeter
video_script.why: A learner sees why adding the same letter twice gives two times the letter.
video_script.substitution: the book's own rectangle with length l and breadth b, checked with l as three and b as four
video_script.anchor: the rectangle of the book with length l and breadth b
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko adds four letters and multiplies them. A letter added to itself gives two times that letter, so the idea is broken with l as five and b as six.
video_script.payoff_line: The perimeter is two l plus two b

final_answer.value: p = 2l + 2b, which is the simplified form; both forms give 14 for l = 3 and b = 4
final_answer.spoken: the perimeter is two l plus two b, and both forms give fourteen

maths_rules: l + l = 2 x l = 2l and b + b = 2 x b = 2b, so p = 2l + 2b
check with l = 3, b = 4: 2 x 3 + 2 x 4 = 6 + 8 = 14
Keeko test: 4 x 5 x 6 = 120, which is not 22
video_script.design: One rectangle stays on the board all video; the sides are added, the same letters are grouped, and the short form is checked with numbers.

beats.on_screen: title card From your book; a rectangle with its length l and its breadth b written on the sides

marks.scene: the title card arrives and the rectangle is drawn
marks.sides: the letters l and b are written on the sides
marks.ask: the four sides light up one by one
marks.shorter: a question mark appears beside the sum

narration: <bookmark mark='scene'/>This is a question from your book about the perimeter of a rectangle.
<bookmark mark='sides'/>The length is the letter-number l, and the breadth is the letter-number b.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>The book wants the perimeter as a sum of the four sides, made shorter.
<bookmark mark='shorter'/>What will the shorter form look like?

beats.on_screen: the rectangle stays on the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: the rectangle with an arrow walking round its edge; the sides in order l, b, l, b

marks.edge: the whole edge of the rectangle lights up
marks.walk: the four sides are named in order as the arrow walks round
marks.order: two terms swap places to show that the order does not matter

narration: <bookmark mark='edge'/>The perimeter is the distance all the way round the edge.
<bookmark mark='walk'/>Walk round the rectangle, and the sides come as l, then b, then l, then b again.
<bookmark mark='order'/>Letter-numbers stand for numbers, so terms can be added in any order.

beats.on_screen: Given: a rectangle, length l, breadth b
narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, a rectangle with length l and breadth b.

beats.on_screen: To find: the perimeter p as a sum, a shorter form, and a check with l = 3, b = 4

marks.find: the words the perimeter p as a sum are written
marks.then: the words shorter form and check are written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to write the perimeter as a sum of the four sides.
<bookmark mark='then'/>Then we make the sum shorter, and check it with l as three and b as four.

beats.on_screen: Step 1, add the four sides: p = l + b + l + b

marks.sum: the heading is written and the four sides are added one by one
marks.line: p = l + b + l + b is written

narration: <bookmark mark='sum'/>Step one, add the four sides in order, because the perimeter is the sum of the sides.
<bookmark mark='line'/>The perimeter p is l plus b plus l plus b.

beats.on_screen: Step 2, swap the terms: p = l + l + b + b

marks.swap: the two b terms and the second l swap places
marks.line: p = l + l + b + b is written under the first line

narration: <bookmark mark='swap'/>Step two, swap the terms, because terms can be added in any order.
<bookmark mark='line'/>That gives l plus l plus b plus b.

beats.on_screen: Step 3, add the same letters: l + l = 2 × l = 2l and b + b = 2 × b = 2b; simplified form 2l + 2b

marks.name: the words simplified form are written beside 2l + 2b

narration: <bookmark mark='join'/>Step three, add the same letters together.
<bookmark mark='ll'/>The sum l plus l is two times l, which is two l.
<bookmark mark='bb'/>The sum b plus b is two times b, which is two b.
<bookmark mark='name'/>We call two l plus two b the simplified form of the sum.

marks.check: the heading is written and 3 and 4 replace l and b
marks.four: the four sides are added as 3 + 4 + 3 + 4 = 14
marks.two: the short form is worked as 2 × 3 + 2 × 4 = 6 + 8 = 14
marks.same: the two totals are joined by an equals sign

narration: <bookmark mark='check'/>Step four, check with l as three and b as four.
<bookmark mark='four'/>The four sides add as three plus four plus three plus four, which is fourteen.
<bookmark mark='two'/>Two l plus two b is two times three plus two times four, so six plus eight.
<bookmark mark='same'/>Both ways give the same total.

beats.on_screen: Answer: p = 2l + 2b, the simplified form. Both forms give 14 for l = 3, b = 4.

marks.both: the number 14 lights up in both lines of the check

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>The perimeter is two l plus two b.
<bookmark mark='both'/>Both forms give fourteen when l is three and b is four.

beats.on_screen: Keeko with a raised hand beside the rectangle
narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: Keeko's bubble: 4 × l × b, struck out; the test l = 5, b = 6 gives 22 and 120

marks.gap: 22 and 120 appear side by side and do not match
marks.fix: the bubble is struck out and 2l + 2b stays

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks the perimeter is four times l times b, because there are four letters.
<bookmark mark='test'/>Try l as five and b as six.
<bookmark mark='gap'/>Adding the four sides gives twenty two, but four times five times six is one hundred and twenty.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>A letter added to itself gives two times that letter, not letters multiplied together.
